CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  February 3, 2020 - 5:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

  OPENING:  Mayor Tomek and President Cahalan called the Special Joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Unified School
  District (PUSD) Board of Education to order at 6:32 p.m. The
  Pledge of Allegiance was led by PUSD President Cahalan.
  (Absent: None)

  ROLL CALL:
  Councilmembers:  Mayor Terry T ornek
  Vice Mayor John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Victor Gordo
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin
  Councilmember Andy Wilson

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky
-  President Patrick Cahalan
  Vice President Scott Phelps
  Member Michelle Richardson Bailey
  Member Roy Boulghourjian
  Member Kimberly Kenne
  Member Elizabeth Pomeroy
  Member Larry Torres

  Staff:  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools
  Leslie Barnes, Ed.D., Chief Business Officer

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Rene Gonzalez, representing PADRES, stated that future
  MULTIPLE AGENDA ITEMS  discussions regarding Roosevelt Elementary School should be
  deferred until such time as the US Department of Education has
  completed its evaluation of the proposed PUSD school closures,
  and also advocated for the school not to be closed.

  PROPOSED ACTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL: PROPOSED
  MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENTS TO UPDATE LOCAL
  SMOKING REGULATIONS AND RESTRICT THE SALE AND
  DISTRIBUTION OF FLAVORED AND MENTHOLATED
  TOBACCO PRODUCTS AND TOBACCO LOOK-ALIKE
  PRODUCTS

  Council Minutes  02/03/2020
   Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to state CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15061 (b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption);
  (2) Direct the City Attorney to prepare amendments to update
  the local Pasadena Municipal Code ("PMC") to align with current
  state and federal definitions related to tobacco products, tobacco
  paraphernalia, tobacco use, and age identification requirements
  and tobacco sales; and prohibit the sale and distribution within
  the city of mentholated cigarettes and/or other flavored tobacco
  products, including flavored products for electronic smoking
  devices ("ESD"), including ESD liquids, flavored little cigars, and
  tobacco look-alike products.
  PROPOSED ACTION OF THE PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT: ADOPT A RESOLUTION ENCOURAGING
  COMMUNITIES TO RESTRICT THE SALE OF FLAVORED
  TOBACCO PRODUCTS AND MENTHOL CIGARETTES
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the Pasadena
  Unified School District, Board of Education adopt a resolution
  encouraging communities to restrict the sale of flavored tobacco
  products and menthol cigarettes.

  Dr. Ying Ying Goh, Director of Public Health, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item, and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember Wilson suggested increasing the severity of
  penalties related to retailers who repeatedly violate the
  prohibition of sale and distribution of mentholated and flavored
  tobacco products.

  Vice Mayor Hampton also requested that the staff
  recommendation include the penalty of a misdemeanor for those
  retailers that violate the updated regulations and restrictions.

  Statice Wilmore, Program Coordinator, responded to questions
  related to Federal legislation and tobacco products, tobacco
  lookalike products, and the retailer license revocation process.

  Councilmember Gordo asked staff to investigate and determine
  the feasibility of the City prohibiting retailers from reapplying for
  a City business license when it has been revoked due to
  violations of the City's tobacco regulations.

  Member Torres requested that PUSD staff work with the City's
  Health Department to develop health lessons, and provide
  accurate and timely information to PUSD students and parents.

Council Minutes  2  02/03/2020
   The following individuals spoke in favor of the item:

  Deidra Duncan, Chair of the Tobacco Prevention Coalition
  Claudia Hathcock, Pasadena resident
  Nancy Verdin, Pasadena resident
  Elizabeth Alvarez, Intern with Day One
  Kaleb Chakarian, with Boys and Girls Club of Pasadena
  Stephanie Barcenas, representing Day One
  Primo Castro, representing American Cancer Society
  Cancer Action Network
  Alisha Lopez, Pasadena resident
  William Meurer, representing Go Green Solutions
  Briana Duncan, Pasadena resident
  Michael Olivares, representing American Lung Association
  Christy Zamani, representing Day One
  Jasmine De La Torre, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation, advocated for a future City Council discussion
  on the possibility of prohibiting the sale of all tobacco products
  in the City, and asked staff to return with an evaluation on the
  City's ability to adopt an ordinance to that effect.

  President Cahalan, spoke in support of the City's proposed
  resolution and amendments.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Kennedy, seconded by Vice Mayor Hampton, to approve the
  staff recommendation, amended to include language in the
  ordinance that labeled violations as misdemeanors, and
  increase the penalties for violations, as follows: first violation
  $500, second violation $1,000, and third violation $2,000 fines.
  (Motion unanimously carried) (Absent: None)

  Following discussion, it was moved by Member Phelps,
  seconded by Member Bailey, that the Board of Education of the
  Pasadena Unified School District adopt a resolution encouraging
  communities to restrict the sale of flavored tobacco products and
  menthol cigarettes. (Motion unanimously carried) (Absent:
  None)

  UPDATE ON THE OFFICE OF THE YOUNG CHILD

  Crystal O'Grady, Early Development Coordinator with Office of
  the Young Child, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the
  Office of the Young Child Master Plan, Early Development
  Instrument (EDI) results, grant funding, partnerships, data
  related to measures of success, and future plans; and
  responded to questions.

Council Minutes  3  02/03/2020
   Councilmember Madison spoke in favor of Measure J funds to

-  be used to fund the Office of the Young Child programs, which
  are measurable, bold and tax dollar accountable.

  Councilmember Gordo asked staff to consider and provide
  information on new strategies to better coordinate with PUSD
  and the Health and Library Departments in order to better inform
  families of the available programs for early childhood education.
  He expressed concerns with the amount of grant funding
  provided by Los Angeles County's Department of Mental Health.
  He requested that a discussion and action be agendized at
  future meetings of the City Council and PUSD to request that LA
  County provide additional funding and/or services for young
  children who attend PUSD schools.

  Elizabeth J. Blanco, Chief Academic Officer, provided
  information on PUSD's funding resources that are used to assist
  and support the Office of the Young Child programs; and
  responded to questions.

  Member Kenne spoke on the need to inform the public that there
  is a percentage of young children that are not ready to enter
  kindergarten.
---  Vice Mayor Hampton requested that staff provide him with
  information on the programs provided by Options for Learning
  and Quality Start Los Angeles so that he can disseminate the
  information to his constituents.

  President Cahalan, spoke on the need for additional marketing
  of the programs offered by the Office of the Young Child and
  requested that distribution lists for such information include the
  members of Board of Education and City Council.

  Councilmember Wilson requested data on the current
  assessment of the Early Development Instrument program
  results related to the City; and strongly encouraged staff to
  consider using the Central Library as a "Growing Together
  Pasadena" site.

  Councilmember Kennedy encouraged Ms. O'Grady to meet with
  Mr. Rene Gonzalez, his appointee on the Human Relations
  Commission, to invite him to participate and focus his student
  advocacy on programs and issues related to the Office of the
  Young Child.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  Council Minutes  4  0210312020
   UPDATE ON YOUTH MASTER PLAN

-  Christy Zamani, Executive Director with Day One, Tony
  Santilena,  representing  Youth  Alley,  and  various
  PUSD/Pasadena City College students, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the Youth Master Plan,
  summarizing the progress report on the various Priority Areas
  and next steps; and responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Hampton requested that in the future, the Update of
  the Youth Master Plan be agendized at the beginning of the joint
  meeting to accommodate PUSD student's school schedule. He
  thanked PUSD for providing PUSD students with healthy and
  appetizing lunch meals. He also spoke on the need for the City's
  Health Department to work with PUSD to develop programs that
  provide safe space areas, as well as mental health support.

  Councilmember Gordo requested information on what mental
  health services are provided to PUSD students; and spoke on
  the need to expose PUSD students to different experiences.

  Member Pomeroy spoke on the need to utilize their Student
  Board Members as a special focus group to determine how
  PUSD can incorporate their insights into future planning.

  Councilmember Madison stated that he believes that the City
  should not charge for local transit for student riders on City
  buses.

  Councilmember Kennedy asked staff to provide information on
  the number of participants in the City's Summer Rose Program
  within the last six years; and determine through the budget
  process, a method where Summer Rose Program participants
  can be placed for work in non-profit organizations in the City.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  UPDATE ON COLLABORATE PASADENA

  Donald E. Grant Jr., Executive Director and Geoff Albert,
  Community Engagement Specialist, representing Collaborate
  Pasadena, distributed information and presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on their organization, partnerships and
  participants, domains of impacts, parent engagement, student
  success, and opportunities; and responded to questions.

  Council Minutes  5  0210312020
   Councilmember Kennedy recommended that Mr. Grant contact
  Ms. Linda Machida, a local grant consultant, who previously
  worked with Collaborate Pasadena, and Mr. Byron Reed, Senior
  Vice President with CIT Bank, who could possibly assist with
  Collaborate Pasadena's grant funding endeavors.

  Vice President Phelps expressed concerns with the
  presentations made at these joint meetings that lack input or
  participation by PUSD staff and that he believes is missing
  information.

  Wayne from Encino, residence not stated, spoke on matters
  related to the Brown Act.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  DISCUSSION OF POTENTIAL FUTURE USES FOR CLOSED
  SCHOOL SITES

  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools, provided
  introductory comments, and Leslie Barnes, Ed.D. Chief
  Business Officer, presented a PowerPoint on PUSD's status of
  several PUSD properties, potential process to sell or dispose of
  these properties, update on PUSD's land swap, and responded
  to questions.

  President Cahalan, President of the PUSD Board, invited City
  staff or a member of the City Council to work with the PUSD's
  proposed 7-11 Committee, to improve communication between
  PUSD and the City Council; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy asked that the 7-11 Committee
  seriously consider and prioritize any future use of surplus
  properties for affordable housing. He also asked for information
  on the guiding laws and regulations governing the selling of
  surplus property in PUSD; and for staff to provide information on
  the schedule of meetings. Councilmember Kennedy stated the
  following for the record, "As one Councilmember, to recommend
  that strong consideration in our distributed policy, related to
  affordable housing, that if there is a possibility, and I suspect
  there is, even if it needs to be re-zoned, that we would look at
  that as a possibility for affordable housing."

  Councilmember McAustin suggested that PUSD meet with state
  legislatures and inform them of these potential affordable
  housing opportunities utilizing surplus property, provide
  information on the proposed sites, and request assistance with
  facilitating and navigating the District though the process.

Council Minutes  6  02/03/2020
   Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns with the timeline for
  the proposed process to dispose of these properties; and also
  noted his concern for selling off property that once gone, could
  not be regained. He pointed out the potential issues with PUSD
  moving forward in repurposing public school properties for other
  uses such as affordable housing without receiving sufficient
  input from the community and/or the City. He spoke on the need
  for a discussion on this issue, as well as a public education
  campaign in the community, so that the School District is
  informed by the public in terms of the appropriateness of
  proceeding with the disposal or repurposing of these properties.

Vice Mayor Hampton was  Councilmember Madison also expressed concern with selling
excused and left the meeting at and irrevocably losing neighborhood school sites.
10:43 p.m.
  Member Bailey spoke in favor of developing housing for PUSD
  staff and expressed concerns with selling school property.

  Councilmember Wilson suggested that staff consider utilizing
  the proposed disposed properties as park areas with soccer
  fields, which would be a good community benefit.

  The following individuals provided comments related to various
  proposed schools sites, affordable housing, retaining PUSD
  staff, advocated for Roosevelt school site not to be closed,
  workforce housing, and/or the need for an analysis of historic
  resources:

  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident
  Janneth Gonzalez, PADRES
  Nina Chomsky, Linda Vista-Annandale Association

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  Mayor Tomek stated the following for the record, "I would like
  the minutes to reflect that when we have our next joint meeting,
  that the kids are first on the agenda and that the PUSD school
  staff make more presentations."

Council Minutes  7  02/03/2020
 ADJOURNMENT  On the order of the President and Mayor, the special joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Board of Education
  adjourned at 11 :29 p.m.
